#![allow(unused, non_snake_case, non_camel_case_types, unreachable_patterns, unreachable_code, clippy::all)]

use super::types;

/// Error returned by procs.
pub type Error = Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync>;

/// The node that failed, wrapping its implementation's error.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct NodeError {
    pub node: &'static str,
    pub source: Error,
}

impl std::fmt::Display for NodeError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "{}: {}", self.node, self.source)
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for NodeError {
    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {
        Some(&*self.source)
    }
}

fn wrap(node: &'static str, source: Error) -> Error {
    Box::new(NodeError { node, source })
}

/// A failure as a program prints it: the error underneath the nodes, and
/// (when it passed through more than one) the nodes, outermost first.
pub fn describe_error(e: &Error) -> String {
    let mut nodes = vec![];
    let mut cur: &(dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static) = &**e;
    while let Some(n) = cur.downcast_ref::<NodeError>() {
        nodes.push(n.node);
        cur = &*n.source;
    }
    if nodes.len() > 1 { format!("{cur}\n  (in {})", nodes.join(" > ")) } else { cur.to_string() }
}

fn get<'a, T>(slot: &'a Option<T>, node: &str) -> Result<&'a T, Error> {
    slot.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| format!("{node} has not run").into())
}

/// Moves a value out of its slot, at its last read.
fn take_slot<T>(slot: &mut Option<T>, node: &str) -> Result<T, Error> {
    slot.take().ok_or_else(|| format!("{node} has not run").into())
}

/// Looks up `k`, failing if it's missing.
fn map_get<K: Ord + std::fmt::Debug, V: Clone>(m: &std::collections::BTreeMap<K, V>, k: &K) -> Result<V, Error> {
    m.get(k).cloned().ok_or_else(|| format!("key {k:?} not found").into())
}

/// Indexes `xs`, failing if `i` is out of range.
fn slice_get<E: Clone>(xs: &[E], i: &i64) -> Result<E, Error> {
    usize::try_from(*i)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|i| xs.get(i).cloned())
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("index {i} out of range [0, {})", xs.len()).into())
}

/// Unoptimized, a proc's frame holds every node's temporaries at once, so
/// grammar-deep recursion overflows the default 2 MiB; debug builds give
/// their threads more.
fn thread_builder() -> std::thread::Builder {
    let b = std::thread::Builder::new();
    #[cfg(debug_assertions)]
    let b = b.stack_size(64 << 20);
    b
}

/// Runs `f` over `xs` on scoped threads; results keep input order.
fn fan_out<E: Send, R: Send>(xs: Vec<E>, f: impl Fn(E) -> Result<R, Error> + Sync) -> Result<Vec<R>, Error> {
    std::thread::scope(|s| {
        let f = &f;
        let handles: Vec<_> = xs
            .into_iter()
            .map(|x| thread_builder().spawn_scoped(s, move || f(x)).expect("cannot spawn a thread"))
            .collect();
        handles
            .into_iter()
            .map(|h| h.join().unwrap_or_else(|p| std::panic::resume_unwind(p)))
            .collect()
    })
}

struct EnvForEach {

    out_for_each_collect: Option<i64>,
    in_for_each_process: Option<InForEachProcess>,
    out_for_each_process: Option<i64>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum PcForEach {
    ForEachStart,
    ForEachCollect,
    ForEachProcess,
}

/// Runs proc ForEach.
pub fn run_for_each(i: i64) -> Result<i64, Error> {
    let mut env = EnvForEach::default();
    env.in_for_each_start = Some(InForEachStart { i: i });
    let mut pc = PcForEach::ForEachStart;
    loop {
        match pc {
            PcForEach::ForEachStart => {
                let input = take_slot(&mut env.in_for_each_start, "ForEach.Start")?;
                let this = unimplemented_for_each_start(input.i).map_err(|e| wrap("ForEach.Start", e.into()))?;
                env.out_for_each_start = Some(this.clone());
                let dim = get(&env.out_for_each_start, "ForEach.Start")?.l.clone();
                let results = fan_out(dim.to_vec(), |elem| run_for_each_region1(env.clone(), elem))?;
                let this = types::List::from(results);
                env.in_for_each_collect = Some(InForEachCollect { l: this });
                pc = PcForEach::ForEachCollect;
                continue;
            }
            PcForEach::ForEachCollect => {
                let input = take_slot(&mut env.in_for_each_collect, "ForEach.Collect")?;
                let this = unimplemented_for_each_collect(input.l).map_err(|e| wrap("ForEach.Collect", e.into()))?;
                return Ok(this);
            }
            _ => return Err(format!("ForEach: invalid state {pc:?}").into()),
        }
    }
}

/// One element of the for each from ForEach.Start.
fn run_for_each_region1(mut env: EnvForEach, elem: i64) -> Result<i64, Error> {
    let this = elem;
    env.in_for_each_process = Some(InForEachProcess { i: this.clone(), l: get(&env.out_for_each_start, "ForEach.Start")?.l.clone() });
    let mut pc = PcForEach::ForEachProcess;
    loop {
        match pc {
            PcForEach::ForEachProcess => {
                let input = take_slot(&mut env.in_for_each_process, "ForEach.Process")?;
                let this = unimplemented_for_each_process(input.i, input.l).map_err(|e| wrap("ForEach.Process", e.into()))?;
                return Ok(this);
            }
            _ => return Err(format!("ForEach: invalid state {pc:?}").into()),
        }
    }
}

    BarStart,
    BarLoop,
    ForEach,
    BarBranch1,
    BarBranch2Begin,
    BarEnd,
    FooCall,
    BarBranch2End,

/// Runs proc Bar.
pub fn run_bar(a: i64, b: types::Str) -> Result<types::Str, Error> {
    let mut env = EnvBar::default();
    env.in_bar_start = Some(InBarStart { a: a, b: b });
    let mut pc = PcBar::BarStart;
    loop {
        match pc {
            PcBar::BarStart => {
                let input = take_slot(&mut env.in_bar_start, "Bar.Start")?;
                let this = unimplemented_bar_start(input.a, input.b).map_err(|e| wrap("Bar.Start", e.into()))?;
                env.out_bar_start = Some(this.clone());
                env.in_bar_loop = Some(InBarLoop { s: this });
                pc = PcBar::BarLoop;
                continue;
            }
            PcBar::BarLoop => {
                let input = take_slot(&mut env.in_bar_loop, "Bar.Loop")?;
                let this = unimplemented_bar_loop(input.s).map_err(|e| wrap("Bar.Loop", e.into()))?;
                if (this.clone() < 10_i64) {
                    env.in_bar_loop = Some(InBarLoop { s: get(&env.out_bar_start, "Bar.Start")?.clone() });
                    pc = PcBar::BarLoop;
                    continue;
                }
                env.in_for_each = Some(InForEachStart { i: this });
                pc = PcBar::ForEach;
                continue;
            }
            PcBar::ForEach => {
                let input = take_slot(&mut env.in_for_each, "ForEach")?;
                let this = run_for_each(input.i).map_err(|e| wrap("ForEach", e.into()))?;
                if (this.clone() == 0_i64) {
                    env.in_bar_branch1 = Some(InBarBranch1 { i: this });
                    pc = PcBar::BarBranch1;
                    continue;
                }
                env.in_bar_branch2_begin = Some(InBarBranch2Begin { i: this });
                pc = PcBar::BarBranch2Begin;
                continue;
            }
            PcBar::BarBranch1 => {
                let input = take_slot(&mut env.in_bar_branch1, "Bar.Branch1")?;
                let this = unimplemented_bar_branch1(input.i).map_err(|e| wrap("Bar.Branch1", e.into()))?;
                env.in_bar_end = Some(InBarEnd { r: types::BarEndR::I(this) });
                pc = PcBar::BarEnd;
                continue;
            }
            PcBar::BarBranch2Begin => {
                let input = take_slot(&mut env.in_bar_branch2_begin, "Bar.Branch2Begin")?;
                let this = unimplemented_bar_branch2_begin(input.i).map_err(|e| wrap("Bar.Branch2Begin", e.into()))?;
                env.in_foo_call = Some(InFooCall { s: this });
                pc = PcBar::FooCall;
                continue;
            }
            PcBar::BarEnd => {
                let input = take_slot(&mut env.in_bar_end, "Bar.End")?;
                let this = unimplemented_bar_end(input.r).map_err(|e| wrap("Bar.End", e.into()))?;
                return Ok(this);
            }
            PcBar::FooCall => {
                let input = take_slot(&mut env.in_foo_call, "Foo.Call")?;
                let this = unimplemented_foo_call(input.s).map_err(|e| wrap("Foo.Call", e.into()))?;
                env.in_bar_branch2_end = Some(InBarBranch2End { i: this });
                pc = PcBar::BarBranch2End;
                continue;
            }
            PcBar::BarBranch2End => {
                let input = take_slot(&mut env.in_bar_branch2_end, "Bar.Branch2End")?;
                let this = unimplemented_bar_branch2_end(input.i).map_err(|e| wrap("Bar.Branch2End", e.into()))?;
                env.in_bar_end = Some(InBarEnd { r: types::BarEndR::S });
                pc = PcBar::BarEnd;
                continue;
            }
            _ => return Err(format!("Bar: invalid state {pc:?}").into()),
        }
    }
}

#![allow(non_camel_case_types, non_snake_case, dead_code)]

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::sync::Arc;

/// A string. Immutable, so a clone shares it.
pub type Str = Arc<str>;

/// An array. Immutable, so a clone shares it. `concat` reuses this one's
/// buffer when nothing else shares it, and copies otherwise. Derefs to a
/// slice.
#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct List<T>(Arc<Vec<T>>);

impl<T> Clone for List<T> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        List(self.0.clone())
    }
}

impl<T> Default for List<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        List(Arc::new(Vec::new()))
    }
}

impl<T> std::ops::Deref for List<T> {
    type Target = [T];
    fn deref(&self) -> &[T] {
        &self.0
    }
}

impl<T> From<Vec<T>> for List<T> {
    fn from(v: Vec<T>) -> Self {
        List(Arc::new(v))
    }
}

impl<T: Clone> From<&[T]> for List<T> {
    fn from(v: &[T]) -> Self {
        List(Arc::new(v.to_vec()))
    }
}

impl<T> FromIterator<T> for List<T> {
    fn from_iter<I: IntoIterator<Item = T>>(iter: I) -> Self {
        List(Arc::new(iter.into_iter().collect()))
    }
}

impl<T: Clone> IntoIterator for List<T> {
    type Item = T;
    type IntoIter = std::vec::IntoIter<T>;
    fn into_iter(self) -> Self::IntoIter {
        Arc::unwrap_or_clone(self.0).into_iter()
    }
}

impl<'a, T> IntoIterator for &'a List<T> {
    type Item = &'a T;
    type IntoIter = std::slice::Iter<'a, T>;
    fn into_iter(self) -> Self::IntoIter {
        self.0.iter()
    }
}

impl<T: std::fmt::Debug> std::fmt::Debug for List<T> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_list().entries(self.iter()).finish()
    }
}

impl<T: Clone> List<T> {
    /// This array's elements, then `other`'s. Appends in place when nothing
    /// else shares this array.
    pub fn concat(mut self, other: &List<T>) -> List<T> {
        Arc::make_mut(&mut self.0).extend_from_slice(other);
        self
    }
}

/// A map. Immutable, so a clone shares it. `merge` and `without` change
/// this one in place when nothing else shares it, and copy otherwise.
/// Derefs to a `BTreeMap`.
#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct Map<K, V>(Arc<BTreeMap<K, V>>);

impl<K, V> Clone for Map<K, V> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        Map(self.0.clone())
    }
}

impl<K, V> Default for Map<K, V> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Map(Arc::new(BTreeMap::new()))
    }
}

impl<K, V> std::ops::Deref for Map<K, V> {
    type Target = BTreeMap<K, V>;
    fn deref(&self) -> &BTreeMap<K, V> {
        &self.0
    }
}

impl<K, V> From<BTreeMap<K, V>> for Map<K, V> {
    fn from(m: BTreeMap<K, V>) -> Self {
        Map(Arc::new(m))
    }
}

impl<K: Ord, V> FromIterator<(K, V)> for Map<K, V> {
    fn from_iter<I: IntoIterator<Item = (K, V)>>(iter: I) -> Self {
        Map(Arc::new(iter.into_iter().collect()))
    }
}

impl<K: Clone, V: Clone> IntoIterator for Map<K, V> {
    type Item = (K, V);
    type IntoIter = std::collections::btree_map::IntoIter<K, V>;
    fn into_iter(self) -> Self::IntoIter {
        Arc::unwrap_or_clone(self.0).into_iter()
    }
}

impl<K: std::fmt::Debug, V: std::fmt::Debug> std::fmt::Debug for Map<K, V> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        self.0.fmt(f)
    }
}

impl<K: Ord + Clone, V: Clone> Map<K, V> {
    /// This map's entries and `other`'s; `other` wins.
    pub fn merge(mut self, other: &Map<K, V>) -> Map<K, V> {
        Arc::make_mut(&mut self.0).extend(other.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.clone())));
        self
    }

    /// This map without `keys`.
    pub fn without(mut self, keys: &[K]) -> Map<K, V> {
        if keys.iter().any(|k| self.0.contains_key(k)) {
            let m = Arc::make_mut(&mut self.0);
            for k in keys {
                m.remove(k);
            }
        }
        self
    }
}
